constraints: Source revision is not deployable artifact identity.
Mutable image tag or alias is not immutable deployment identity.
QA strategy success is not equivalent to QualityAcceptance ACCEPT.
A caller-selected subset of component refs cannot prove acceptance completeness.
Deployment change during the QA verification window cannot produce current acceptance for the newer release.
DevOps and Product QA remain separate authority domains for deployment publication and quality judgment.

deployment change during QA cannot produce current acceptance for newer release

architectureDecisions: DeployableArtifactRef pins component + immutable artifact digest; BuildProvenance links it to accepted source delivery. Commit/tag are metadata, not deployable identity.
BB-054 may research BB-053's READY plan, but WORKER waits for BB-053 DONE and then consumes delivered current truth, never the plan as runtime authority.
DevOps uses DomainExecutionController with a DEVOPS WorkContract/input; strategy success is deployment evidence, not quality acceptance.
DeploymentRelease is immutable and requires accepted DevOps completion/publication plus exact FE/BE deployables, environment/config and rollout evidence.
DeploymentReleaseHead(environmentRef) is CAS currentness with one mutation guard shared by release publication and QA final-currentness validation.
AcceptanceSnapshot is deterministic from one current DeploymentRelease + acceptance policy; mandatory FE/BE refs and verifier policy are derived, not caller-selected.
RuntimeObservationEvidence comes from an independent observer and binds expected vs observed runtime identities; self-report is insufficient.
Mixed/unknown/mismatched runtime identities are non-accepted by default unless the pinned policy explicitly permits a bounded set.
QA execution binds one snapshot and emits evidence only; QualityAcceptance requires separate ACCEPT completion/publication authority.
Final QualityAcceptance holds the exact release-head guard, so deployment drift during QA cannot become current acceptance.
Release/snapshot/observation/acceptance artifacts remain immutable and resolvable after current heads advance.
implementationSlices: EF1 — Provenance [AC-1, AC-7, INV-1, INV-2]: add immutable BuildProvenance + DeployableArtifactRef; require FRONTEND/BACKEND, accepted sourceDeliveryRef, artifactDigest and build evidence; commit/tag alone fail. Verify deployable-provenance + deployment-provenance-chain.

EF2 — Release [AC-1, AC-5, AC-6, INV-8]: DEVOPS consumes exact delivered domain input; accepted DevOps completion/publication creates immutable DeploymentRelease and CAS-advances DeploymentReleaseHead(environmentRef) under one mutation guard. Verify deployment-release + domain-execution-regression.

EF3 — Snapshot [AC-2, AC-6, INV-6]: deterministically derive AcceptanceSnapshot from exact current release + policy; pin release/head revision, FE/BE refs, environment, criteria and verifier policy; expose no caller component subset. Verify acceptance-snapshot.

EF4 — Observation [AC-3, AC-4, INV-3]: independent observer emits RuntimeObservationEvidence per required component; unknown/mixed/mismatched identity is non-accepted unless pinned policy permits the bounded set. Verify runtime-observation.

EF5 — QA authority [AC-3, AC-4, AC-7, INV-4, INV-5, INV-8]: QA binds one snapshot, prechecks release currentness and emits evidence only; separate publisher requires ACCEPT DomainCompletionDecision + DomainPublicationReceipt for QualityAcceptance. Verify product-qa + existing acceptance/execution regressions.

EF6 — Race fence [AC-5, INV-7]: final publisher reacquires and holds the exact DeploymentReleaseHead guard through QualityAcceptance current-head CAS; pre-lock drift fails and concurrent DevOps head advancement cannot cross the commit. Verify product-qa-race.

EF7 — Reconstruction [AC-6, AC-7]: persist with existing immutable/CAS primitives and resolve SourceDelivery -> BuildProvenance -> Deployable -> Release -> Snapshot -> Observation -> QualityAcceptance in a fresh process. Verify deployment-provenance-chain.
